title: Firefox add-on (addons.mozilla.org)
appliesWhen: A browser extension for Firefox, listed on addons.mozilla.org (AMO) or self-distributed after Mozilla signing.
ask: Will the extension be published on addons.mozilla.org (listed) or self-distributed (unlisted), and does it collect or transmit any user data?
guidance: web-ext lint runs the same addons-linter checks as AMO upload validation. It exits non-zero on errors; warnings fail only with --warnings-as-errors. A manifest declaring both background.scripts and background.service_worker (the cross-browser pattern) gets a BACKGROUND_SERVICE_WORKER_IGNORED warning, so leave -w off for shared manifests or lint a Firefox-specific build.
An add-on ID in browser_specific_settings.gecko.id is required to publish an MV3 extension (web-ext lint reports ADDON_ID_REQUIRED otherwise).

From 3 November 2025 every new extension must declare browser_specific_settings.gecko.data_collection_permissions, using "required": ["none"] if nothing is collected or transmitted. Existing add-ons will need it for new versions later. web-ext lint warns when it is missing.

Data categories: personal data types (personallyIdentifyingInfo, healthInfo, financialAndPaymentInfo, authenticationInfo, personalCommunications, locationInfo, browsingActivity, websiteContent, websiteActivity, searchTerms, bookmarksInfo) may be required or optional; technicalAndInteraction must be optional. Optional types are requested later with permissions.request() from a user action and can be toggled in about:addons.

Built-in consent works from Firefox 140 desktop and 142 Android. For new extensions, set strict_min_version to 140 (gecko) and 142 (gecko_android), or turn off data collection on older versions; otherwise you must build your own consent screen shown right after install.
Policy on data: transmit only what the functionality needs; personal data needs explicit opt-in; technical and interaction data must be declinable without losing functionality.

Source code: if any file is minified, bundled, transpiled or generated (webpack, Vite, Rollup, TypeScript, templates), upload the original source with a README giving OS, tool versions and exact build commands, plus the lockfile. Reviewers build it and diff the result against the package; there must be no differences. Build tools must be open source and run locally (no web-based tools). Source uploads are limited to 200 MB.
Obfuscated code and remote code are not allowed; minification is. Add-ons must not weaken web pages' security headers such as their Content-Security-Policy.

Listing: describe what the add-on does and what data it transmits, disclose any paid features, and make unexpected features opt-in. Injected ads must be labelled as coming from the add-on; no affiliate-tag injection or redirection, no cryptocurrency mining.
Firefox host permissions (from Firefox 127) are shown and granted at install, but users can revoke any host permission later; check and request them when needed.

gates.title: web-ext lint: no errors
gates.setup: npm install --save-dev web-ext; build the Firefox package into dist/ (or change the folder with profile gate G-FF-LINT --command "npx web-ext lint --source-dir <folder>").
gates.architecture: Record the Firefox build (which folder is the Firefox package, the gecko id, strict_min_version for desktop and Android) and whether warnings are also enforced.
acceptance: web-ext lint reports 0 errors for the Firefox package
Remaining warnings are listed in the task with the reason each is accepted

gates.title: Data collection declared in the manifest and consented to
gates.architecture: Record the data_collection_permissions (required and optional categories, or "none"), the feature behind each category, how optional categories are requested (permissions.request from a user action), and the minimum Firefox versions or the fallback consent for older versions.
acceptance: browser_specific_settings.gecko.data_collection_permissions lists every category the add-on transmits, or "required": ["none"] when it transmits nothing
Nothing in an optional category is sent until the user grants it, and revoking it in about:addons stops the transmission, with tests
technicalAndInteraction, if used, is optional and declining it does not restrict functionality

gates.title: Reproducible build and source code package for review
gates.architecture: Record the build tools and versions (open source, run locally), the build command, and how the source archive with README and lockfile is produced for each submission.
acceptance: A clean checkout built with the README instructions produces files identical to the submitted package (diff is empty)
The source archive includes the README with OS, Node and npm versions and exact commands, the lockfile, and any private dependencies

gates.title: Add-on policies: listing, monetisation and page security
gates.architecture: Record the listing description, which data the add-on transmits as stated in the listing, any paid features, and any changes the add-on makes to web pages.
acceptance: The listing describes what the add-on does, the data it transmits and any paid features
Unexpected features are described and opt-in; injected content and ads are labelled as coming from the add-on
The add-on does not relax web page security headers such as Content-Security-Policy and does not inject affiliate tags
